A few friends dragged me out to a karaoke bar downtown.
They promised it would just be a casual, low-key night, no pressure, just some drinks and a few embarrassing songs among friends.
What nobody mentioned, apparently, was that the bar was hosting an actual amateur singing competition that night.
There was an actual panel of judges sitting at a table right in front of the small stage.
I found this out precisely when my friend, without asking, submitted my name on the sign-up sheet.
She claimed it would be "hilarious," which is friend-speak for "I want to watch you suffer a little."
I tried to argue my way off the list.
I genuinely pleaded with the host at one point, but apparently sign-ups were final the second a name got written down, no exceptions, no matter how convincingly I begged.
By the time they called my name, I'd had exactly one drink and zero preparation.
I found myself walking up to a stage with actual stage lighting, facing judges who looked unsettlingly serious about karaoke, clipboards and all, like this was some kind of televised singing show.
I picked a song I sort of knew and missed the very first note by a mile.
I just decided to commit fully to the chaos instead of trying to salvage any shred of dignity at that point.
The crowd, to my surprise, loved it.
They cheered louder the worse I got, especially during one dramatic note I attempted that came out somewhere between a yodel and a dying smoke alarm.
By the second chorus, half the room was on their feet, phones out, filming the whole disaster like it was the highlight of their entire week.
Honestly, it might genuinely have been.
The judges gave me a score that was, generously, mediocre.
But one judge said my "commitment to the bit" deserved bonus points, and I've decided to take that as the highest compliment of my adult life.
I didn't win anything, not even close.
But I got a free drink from the bar just for, in the bartender's words, "having the guts to keep going after that first note," which felt like a strangely fitting consolation prize.
Now, whenever karaoke comes up, my friends immediately bring up that night.
Honestly, at this point, I've fully accepted my reputation as someone who will absolutely commit to a bad decision once it's already happening.
Someone actually found the phone footage a few weeks later and sent it to our group chat.
Watching it back, I genuinely couldn't decide whether to be proud or slightly horrified at how confidently I'd committed to every single wrong note.
